summary: E2E frontend validation of the Classification Self-Check 3-step WIZARD at /ai-tools/classification-self-check as cathy@example.com (Family, active). All acceptance criteria met: premium ToolHero renders (data-testid tool-hero-classification-self-check); stepper renders 3 steps (csc-step-care/home/health) and step-3 is reachable by clicking the stepper; Step 1 shows Q1-Q4 + csc-current prefilled to '4' from Dorothy + csc-current-prefilled hint; Step 2 shows Q5-Q9 only (Q1 & Q10 correctly hidden); Step 3 shows Q10-Q16 with csc-submit visible and csc-wizard-next NOT present on the last step; Back is disabled on step 1; csc-submit stays disabled until all 16 answered and csc-cta-help correctly shows the remaining count ('7 questions still to answer'); progress bar updates across steps (25% → 100%); after submitting, csc-result, csc-result-header, csc-wayly-summary, csc-comparison, and csc-actions all render. issues: Dev-only React hydration warning: '<span> cannot be a child of <option>'. The console shows the ve-runtime editor wrapping the interpolated 'Classification {n}' text inside a <span> injected into each <option>. This appears to be an editor/tooling instrumentation artefact around line ClassificationCheck.jsx:1040, not app code. Confirm it does not leak into the production bundle; if it does, wrap the number in a stable text node (e.g. use a template string {`Classification ${n}`}) to avoid the injected span.

rca of the issue: No blocking issue found. The observed hydration warning is caused by the preview environment's ve-runtime injecting a <span data-ve-dynamic> around the '{n}' expression inside the <option>Classification {n}</option> template at ClassificationCheck.jsx:1040. HTML disallows <span> inside <option>, hence React logs the warning. Because it comes from the editor instrumentation (x-ve-dynamic attributes), it likely does not affect production, but the safest fix is to keep the option's child a single text node: `<option key={n} value={n}>{`Classification ${n}`}</option>`.
